text.text: The Atari 5200 was released in 1982 as the successor to the Atari 2600. It was based on Atari's 8-bit computer hardware and was designed to compete with systems such as the ColecoVision and Intellivision. The console introduced analog controllers with numeric keypads and expanded versions of several arcade games. Its library included titles such as Pac-Man, Missile Command, Defender, Star Wars, and Qix. Despite having more advanced hardware than the Atari 2600, the system faced criticism for its controller design and lack of compatibility with existing Atari 2600 games. The Atari 5200 was discontinued in 1984 after a short commercial life. Some of its technology later influenced Atari's 8-bit computer line and future console development.
